@graph.headline: How to Stop Revenge Trading After a Loss: The Loss-Side Protocol
@graph.description: A pre-commitment loss protocol to stop revenge trading: cooldown, session stop, halved size, and a re-entry checklist - mechanical rules, not willpower.

mainEntity.name: How do I stop revenge trading after a loss?

acceptedAnswer.text: With mechanical rules, not willpower: a mandatory 15-30 minute cooldown after any loss (away from screens), a session stop after 2 consecutive losses or at your daily loss budget, and halved position size when you return. These interrupt the emotional surge before it can dictate action. Willpower is not a system; a pre-commitment contract is.

The attempt to recover a loss quickly by entering a new position - frequently larger than normal and often without a valid setup. The defining fact: revenge sequences commonly multiply the original loss and rarely restore it. The loss gets filed mentally as a debt the market owes, and every new trade becomes "collection."

The bias stack: loss aversion makes a loss feel roughly twice as impactful as an equal-sized gain; recency bias overweights the last trade; the illusion of control says you can force the market to comply; the sunk cost fallacy says the money already lost must be "earned back." Once these activate, instinct overwrites the system.

mainEntity.name: Should I stop trading after a big loss?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. A session-stop circuit breaker is one of the highest-leverage habits a trader can build - journaled traders consistently report that stopping early costs the least and saves the most. The market will be there tomorrow; your impaired judgment will not be. A loss day ends when your loss protocol says it ends - not when you feel calm again.

mainEntity.name: How long should I wait before trading again after a loss?

acceptedAnswer.text: A minimum of 15-30 minutes for day traders (longer for higher timeframes); two consecutive losses means the session is over. The clock matters less than the circuit: you are not waiting to feel calm, you are waiting for the plan to be in charge again.

mainEntity.name: How do I know if I'm revenge trading or taking a real setup?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ask yourself: would you take this exact trade, at this exact size, if the previous trade had been a winner? If the answer depends on what happened before, the loss is trading, not you. Every plan criterion must be met - not "it looks good."
